# Tutorial 4 — Climate Stress-Test Experiment

> **Prerequisites**
>
> This tutorial builds on [Tutorial
> 3](https://tanerumit.github.io/ipdcstorm/articles/tutorial_3_climate_change.qmd).
> You should already be familiar with
> [`make_hazard_cfg()`](https://tanerumit.github.io/ipdcstorm/reference/make_hazard_cfg.md),
> [`run_hazard_model()`](https://tanerumit.github.io/ipdcstorm/reference/run_hazard_model.md),
> and named KNMI’23 climate scenarios.

This tutorial shows how to design a **climate stress-test experiment**:
pick a handful of high-impact synthetic years from a long stationary
baseline, then replay those *same* years under future-climate scenarios
using common random numbers (CRN). The result is a directly comparable
set of daily wind traces where any difference between baseline and
future is attributable to climate forcing alone.

> **Two stress-test variants**
>
> This tutorial uses the **filter-based** variant: generate a large
> random ensemble, then pick years whose site-level peak wind exceeds an
> IRMA-like threshold. It is the simplest entry point and runs quickly.
>
> The package also ships an **anchored-pool** variant (recommended for
> production) as the example script
> `inst/extcode/05-stress-test-experiment.R`. It forces every baseline
> year to contain a major historical hurricane drawn from a fixed pool
> (Irma, Maria, Hugo, Luis, Lenny, Georges), adds stochastic per-year
> jitter to timing/intensity/radius via the `pin_jitter` argument of
> [`generate_daily_hazard_impact_spatial()`](https://tanerumit.github.io/ipdcstorm/reference/generate_daily_hazard_impact_spatial.md),
> applies HAZUS-style state-dependent damage amplification, and uses
> `compute_compound_stress_year_metrics()` with a 90-day compound
> window. See the script for the full workflow — the helpers live in
> `R/stress_test_helpers.R` and are accessed via
> `ipdcstorm:::.<name>()`.

## 1 What This Tutorial Covers

By the end, you will be able to:

- generate a long stationary baseline and rate years on a composite
  stress score
- pick representative high-impact years at fixed severity quantiles
  (Q50–Q99)
- replay those year indices under KNMI’23 scenarios with CRN, pinning
  the dominant event
- visualize baseline-vs-scenario daily wind traces in a single faceted
  panel

``` r
library(ipdcstorm)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## 2 Experiment Configuration

A small block of switches controls the entire experiment. The defaults
below run quickly for the vignette; for a production stress-test, raise
`n_sim` to 2,000 or more.

``` r
seed            <- 42L
n_sim           <- 500L                       # raise to 2000+ in production
irma_wind_kt    <- 80                         # IRMA-like site-level threshold (kt)
quantile_probs  <- c(0.50, 0.80, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99)
knmi_scenarios  <- c("knmi_Ld", "knmi_Hd")    # low-dry and high-dry KNMI'23
target_year     <- 2100                       # 2050 (near-term) or 2100 (end-of-century)

# Composite rating weights (must sum to 1)
w_peak   <- 0.5   # severity (max site-level peak wind)
w_damage <- 0.5   # accumulation (integrated portfolio damage)

targets <- tibble::tribble(
  ~name,         ~lat,     ~lon,
  "St_Martin",   18.0708, -63.0501,
  "Saba",        17.6350, -63.2300,
  "Statia",      17.4890, -62.9740,
  "Puerto_Rico", 18.4655, -66.1057,
  "Miami",       25.7617, -80.1918
)

ibtracs_demo <- system.file("extdata", "ibtracs_demo.csv", package = "ipdcstorm")
```

## 3 Part 1 — Baseline & Year Selection

We first run a stationary baseline of `n_sim` synthetic years and
downscale every year to daily wind and damage at every target location.

``` r
cfg_base <- make_hazard_cfg(
  data_path        = ibtracs_demo,
  simulation_years = n_sim,
  climate          = make_climate_cfg(scenario = "stationary")
)

out_base <- run_hazard_model(cfg_base, targets = targets, seed = seed, verbose = FALSE)

daily_base_list <- generate_daily_hazard_impact_spatial(
  out         = out_base,
  location    = targets$name,
  sim_years   = seq_len(n_sim),
  year0       = 2000L,
  gust_factor = 1.0,
  damage      = list(method = "intensity"),
  pulse_shape = "cosine",
  scenario    = "baseline",
  seed        = seed
)
```

> **Including trade-wind background in stress tests**
>
> Pass a
> [`make_background_wind_cfg()`](https://tanerumit.github.io/ipdcstorm/reference/make_background_wind_cfg.md)
> object to
> [`make_hazard_cfg()`](https://tanerumit.github.io/ipdcstorm/reference/make_hazard_cfg.md)
> to fill non-storm days with realistic wind speeds across all
> stress-test replays. Because it is stored in `cfg`, it is embedded in
> every `out` object and picked up automatically by each
> [`generate_daily_hazard_impact_spatial()`](https://tanerumit.github.io/ipdcstorm/reference/generate_daily_hazard_impact_spatial.md)
> call — both the baseline above and all scenario replays below — with
> no extra arguments required. This keeps the CRN isolation intact: the
> background wind is generated with `seed + 1`, so the storm-sampling
> RNG is unaffected. See [Tutorial 1 §Background
> Wind](https://tanerumit.github.io/ipdcstorm/articles/tutorial_1_setup.qmd#sec-background-wind)
> for a full example.

### 3.1 Annual metrics across all sites

Each year is summarised on basin-wide metrics: peak site-level wind,
hurricane- and storm-day counts, and integrated damage across all sites.

``` r
daily_base <- bind_rows(daily_base_list, .id = "location")

annual_all <- daily_base |>
  group_by(sim_year, location) |>
  summarise(
    peak_wind_kt = max(wind_kt, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_hur_days   = sum(wind_kt >= 64, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_storm_days = sum(wind_kt >= 34, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_damage = sum(damage_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  group_by(sim_year) |>
  summarise(
    peak_wind_max    = max(peak_wind_kt),
    hur_days_total   = sum(n_hur_days),
    storm_days_total = sum(n_storm_days),
    damage_total     = sum(total_damage),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

### 3.2 Composite stress rating

Candidate years must contain at least one IRMA-class event (peak wind ≥
80 kt). Surviving years are rank-normalised on two metrics and combined
into a single rating in `[0, 1]`:

| Metric | Meaning |
|----|----|
| `r_peak` | Worst single-site peak wind (severity; loss scales ~wind³). |
| `r_damage` | Sum of `damage_rate` across days and sites (integrated impact). |

``` r
irma_candidates <- annual_all |>
  filter(peak_wind_max >= irma_wind_kt)

n_cand <- nrow(irma_candidates)

irma_rated <- irma_candidates |>
  mutate(
    r_peak   = rank(peak_wind_max, ties.method = "average") / n_cand,
    r_damage = rank(damage_total,  ties.method = "average") / n_cand,
    rating   = w_peak * r_peak + w_damage * r_damage
  ) |>
  arrange(rating)

# Pick years at the target quantiles of the rating distribution
sel_pos      <- pmax(1L, ceiling(quantile_probs * n_cand))
selected_ids <- irma_rated$sim_year[sel_pos]

irma_rated |>
  filter(sim_year %in% selected_ids) |>
  mutate(
    quantile = paste0("Q", round(quantile_probs * 100), "%")
  ) |>
  select(quantile, sim_year, peak_wind_max, hur_days_total,
         damage_total, rating)
```

    #> # A tibble: 5 × 6
    #>   quantile sim_year peak_wind_max hur_days_total damage_total rating
    #>   <chr>       <int>         <dbl>          <int>        <dbl>  <dbl>
    #> 1 Q50%           98         100.0              6       0.0313  0.444
    #> 2 Q80%          444         116.              12       0.0924  0.770
    #> 3 Q90%           80         150.              11       0.0735  0.893
    #> 4 Q95%          257         150.              16       0.0775  0.920
    #> 5 Q99%          332         150.              14       0.120   0.950

### 3.3 Pin the focal event

For each selected year we identify the SID of the basin-level peak
hurricane day. Pinning this SID into every scenario run guarantees the
focal event always appears, with its intensity and duration perturbed by
the scenario’s `delta_sst` — all other storm slots remain free to vary
with climate.

``` r
baseline_stress <- lapply(daily_base_list, function(df) {
  df[df$sim_year %in% selected_ids, ]
})

focal_sids <- setNames(vector("list", length(selected_ids)),
                       as.character(selected_ids))

for (yr in selected_ids) {
  yr_hur <- bind_rows(lapply(baseline_stress, function(df) {
    df[df$sim_year == yr & !is.na(df$event_id) & df$wind_kt >= 64, ]
  }))
  if (nrow(yr_hur) == 0L) {
    focal_sids[[as.character(yr)]] <- NA_character_
    next
  }
  peak_row <- yr_hur[which.max(yr_hur$wind_kt), ]
  focal_sids[[as.character(yr)]] <- sub("_y[0-9]+_[0-9]+$", "",
                                        peak_row$event_id[1L])
}

focal_sids
```

## 4 Part 2 — KNMI’23 Climate Replays

The same `seed` and the same `sim_years = 1:n_sim` vector are used for
every scenario. This is the **common random numbers** trick: the RNG is
consumed at exactly the same rate in every run, so year `i` in the
baseline corresponds to year `i` in the scenario. Differences between
traces therefore isolate climate forcing rather than sampling noise.

> **Why iterate the full `1:n_sim`?**
>
> Passing only `selected_ids` to the scenario run would put its first
> iteration at the initial RNG state, while the baseline reached those
> same indices after consuming hundreds of prior draws. The result would
> be completely different event sampling — unrelated to climate.

``` r
cc_stress <- vector("list", length(knmi_scenarios))
names(cc_stress) <- knmi_scenarios

for (scen in knmi_scenarios) {
  cfg_cc <- make_hazard_cfg(
    data_path        = ibtracs_demo,
    simulation_years = n_sim,
    climate          = make_climate_cfg(scenario   = scen,
                                        target_year = target_year,
                                        perturb     = TRUE)
  )

  out_cc <- run_hazard_model(cfg_cc, targets = targets,
                             seed = seed, verbose = FALSE)

  cc_daily_all <- generate_daily_hazard_impact_spatial(
    out         = out_cc,
    location    = targets$name,
    sim_years   = seq_len(n_sim),
    year0       = 2000L,
    gust_factor = 1.0,
    damage      = list(method = "intensity"),
    pulse_shape = "cosine",
    scenario    = scen,
    seed        = seed,
    pinned_sids = focal_sids
  )

  cc_stress[[scen]] <- lapply(cc_daily_all, function(df) {
    df[df$sim_year %in% selected_ids, ]
  })
}
```

## 5 Part 3 — Visualize the Stress-Test Traces

Each panel below is one selected year, with the stationary baseline
(black) overlaid against the KNMI’23 scenarios (blue = low-dry, red =
high-dry). Reference dashes mark the tropical-storm (34 kt) and
hurricane (64 kt) thresholds.

``` r
focal_location <- "Saba"

scenario_labels <- c(
  "Baseline" = "Baseline (stationary)",
  "knmi_Ld"  = "KNMI L-d (low warming, dry)",
  "knmi_Hd"  = "KNMI H-d (high warming, dry)"
)
scenario_colors <- c(
  "Baseline" = "black",
  "knmi_Ld"  = "#4575b4",
  "knmi_Hd"  = "#d73027"
)

# Hurricane season window (Jun 1 – Dec 31, non-leap)
season_doy_start <- 152L
season_doy_end   <- 365L
month_doy_all    <- cumsum(c(1L, 31L, 28L, 31L, 30L, 31L,
                             30L, 31L, 31L, 30L, 31L, 30L))
season_months    <- 6:12
month_doy_starts <- month_doy_all[season_months]
month_labels     <- month.abb[season_months]

base_df <- baseline_stress[[focal_location]] |>
  mutate(scenario = "Baseline")

knmi_df <- bind_rows(lapply(knmi_scenarios, function(scen) {
  cc_stress[[scen]][[focal_location]] |>
    mutate(scenario = scen)
}))

trace_labels <- setNames(
  paste0("Trace ", seq_along(selected_ids),
         "  \u2014  Q", round(quantile_probs * 100), "%"),
  as.character(selected_ids)
)

plot_df <- bind_rows(knmi_df, base_df) |>
  filter(doy >= season_doy_start, doy <= season_doy_end) |>
  mutate(
    scenario    = factor(scenario, levels = c(knmi_scenarios, "Baseline")),
    trace_label = factor(trace_labels[as.character(sim_year)],
                         levels = trace_labels)
  )
```

``` r
ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = doy, y = wind_kt)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 34, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "#E69F00", linewidth = 0.35, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 64, linetype = "dashed",
             colour = "#d73027", linewidth = 0.35, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_line(data = ~ filter(.x, scenario != "Baseline"),
            aes(colour = scenario), linewidth = 0.9, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_line(data = ~ filter(.x, scenario == "Baseline"),
            aes(colour = scenario), linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = scenario_colors,
                      labels = scenario_labels,
                      breaks = c("Baseline", knmi_scenarios),
                      name   = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(season_doy_start, season_doy_end),
                     breaks = month_doy_starts,
                     labels = month_labels,
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0.01, 0.01))) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  facet_wrap(~ trace_label, nrow = 5, ncol = 1, scales = "fixed") +
  labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = "Sustained wind speed (kt)",
    title = sprintf("%s \u2014 Stress-test wind traces: baseline vs KNMI\u201923",
                    focal_location),
    subtitle = sprintf(
      "%d high-impact years from %d synthetic years (seed = %d, target year %d)",
      length(selected_ids), n_sim, seed, target_year),
    caption = "Dashed: TS (34 kt, orange) and hurricane (64 kt, red) thresholds"
  ) +
  theme_light(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    legend.position  = "bottom",
    legend.key.width = unit(1.4, "cm"),
    strip.text       = element_text(size = 8.5, face = "bold"),
    panel.spacing.y  = unit(0.4, "lines"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(size = 8, colour = "grey40"),
    plot.caption     = element_text(size = 7, colour = "grey50", hjust = 0)
  ) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 1,
                               override.aes = list(linewidth = 1.1)))
```

## 6 Where to Go Next

- Switch `target_year` to `2050` to compare near-term vs end-of-century
  forcing.
- Add `knmi_Ln` / `knmi_Hn` to `knmi_scenarios` for the wet variants.
- Tune `w_peak` / `w_damage` to bias year selection toward severity vs
  accumulation.
- Change `focal_location` to view the same experiment from a different
  island.
- For a production run, point `data_path` at the full IBTrACS NA CSV and
  raise `n_sim` to ≥ 2,000.
